title: Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE — 4.3.1 Grammar in Use: Word Classes (Pronouns)

PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Pronouns are words that stand in for names of people and things. In this sub-strand you will identify personal pronouns used as subjects and objects, and possessive pronouns that show who something belongs to. You will use them in sentences about first aid and about parts of a vehicle near a bridge.

## Strand 4.0: Accidents - First Aid
Sub-strand 4.3.1: Grammar in Use: Word Classes (Pronouns)
Suggested lessons: 3

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) identify personal and possessive pronouns used as subjects and objects for communication
b) use personal and possessive pronouns as subject and object correctly for self- expression
c) adopt the use of personal and possessive pronouns in communication

## What this sub-strand covers
• Personal pronouns
• Possessive pronouns

## Key inquiry questions
1. Which words replace names of people or things in sentences?
2. Which words do we use to show that something belongs to us?

## Core competencies
• Communication and Collaboration: This is promoted as the learner is able to construct sentences orally with peers.
• Self-efficacy: It is developed as the learner gains confidence and high self-esteem when working individually to type personal and possessive pronouns on a word processor, mobile device or tablet

## Values
• Responsibility: It is developed as the learner takes up assigned tasks when discuss pictures on the theme using personal and possessive pronouns collaboratively.
• Unity: It is promoted as learners work jointly to read a newspaper, magazine or poem among others, to identify personal and possessive pronouns

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• ICT: This is promoted as the learner is able to use digital devices to access information online during research on personal and possessive pronouns.

## Links to other learning areas
• The learner is able to connect the concept of personal safety and first aid to their learning of similar concepts in Science and Technology.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 English Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Theme 4.0 Accidents- First Aid, Sub-strand 4.3.1 Word classes: Pronouns

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: Personal pronouns as subjects and objects

LESSON 1: PERSONAL PRONOUNS AS SUBJECTS AND OBJECTS
===================================================

## What you will learn
• Identify personal pronouns that do the action and personal pronouns that receive it.
• Replace a noun with the correct subject or object pronoun.
• Correct sentences that use me or I in the wrong place.

Curriculum outcomes: a) identify personal and possessive pronouns used as subjects and objects for communication; b) use personal and possessive pronouns as subject and object correctly for self- expression

## Introduction
Amina helped Juma. She helped him. The second sentence is shorter because she and him stand in for the names. Choosing the wrong pronoun makes the sentence sound unfinished or rude to the ear.

## Notes
### What a personal pronoun does
A personal pronoun takes the place of a person or a thing that has already been named. There are two jobs to learn.

The subject pronoun does the action. It comes before the verb.

- I, you, he, she, it, we, they

The object pronoun receives the action, or comes after a word such as to, for, with or near.

- me, you, him, her, it, us, them

Notice that you and it stay the same. The others change.

### Matching the pronoun
- Amina washed the cut. She washed it.
- The nurse helped Juma. The nurse helped him.
- The teacher called Amina and Juma. The teacher called them.
- Otieno and I carried the kit. We carried it.

Use he, him and his for a boy or a man, she and her for a girl or a woman, and it for one thing or animal when we are not using a personal name. Use they and them for more than one person or thing.

### Two mistakes to avoid
The subject form is I, not me. Say Amina and I saw the bridge, not Me and Amina saw the bridge. Put the other person first: Amina and I, not I and Amina.

The object form is me, him, her, us or them, not the subject form. Say The nurse helped me, not The nurse helped I. Say The motorcycle nearly hit him, not The motorcycle nearly hit he.

### A short scene
Chebet fell near the bridge and cut her knee. Wanjiru ran to her. 'I will call the teacher,' Wanjiru said. The teacher knelt beside them and opened the first aid kit. 'We will clean it,' she said. She did not give them any medicine. An adult does that, if it is needed.

## Key words
• pronoun — a word that takes the place of a noun, such as she or them
• subject pronoun — a pronoun that does the action, such as I, he, she, we or they
• object pronoun — a pronoun that receives the action, such as me, him, her, us or them
• verb — the action word in a sentence, such as helped or washed

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Replace the underlined names: Amina showed Juma the footbridge.

Working:
1. Amina does the action, so use she.
2. Juma receives the showing, so use him.

Answer: She showed him the footbridge.

### Example 2
Choose the correct word: The driver gave the warning to (we / us).

Working:
1. The pronoun comes after to, so it is an object.
2. The object form of we is us.

Answer: The driver gave the warning to us.

### Example 3
Correct this sentence: Me and Otieno told the teacher.

Working:
1. Me cannot be the subject.
2. Name the other person first, then use I.

Answer: Otieno and I told the teacher.

## Activity: Pronouns in a picture talk
You will need: A picture of children near a bridge, with a car and an adult, Sentence strips
1. In groups, look at the picture and name the people and things.
2. Say four sentences about the picture. Each sentence must use a subject pronoun and, where you can, an object pronoun.
3. Write the sentences and underline the pronouns. Mark S for a subject pronoun and O for an object pronoun.
4. Read one sentence aloud and let the group say whether the pronoun is in the right place.

## Practice
1. Write the object pronoun that matches she.
2. Replace the nouns: The doctor examined the patient.
3. Which is correct: 'Them are at the crossing' or 'They are at the crossing'?
4. Fill in: The teacher praised ____ (I / me) for getting help.

## Summary
• Subject pronouns do the action: I, you, he, she, it, we, they.
• Object pronouns receive the action: me, you, him, her, it, us, them.
• Say 'Amina and I', and say 'helped me', not 'helped I'.

### Answers to practice
1. her
2. He examined him, or She examined her, or The doctor examined him or her. A correct pair is: She examined him.
3. They are at the crossing. They is the subject pronoun.
4. me

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: Possessive pronouns

LESSON 2: POSSESSIVE PRONOUNS
=============================

## What you will learn
• Tell a possessive pronoun from a word like my or our that needs a noun.
• Use possessive pronouns as the subject or the object of a sentence.
• Choose its or it's correctly.

Curriculum outcomes: a) identify personal and possessive pronouns used as subjects and objects for communication; b) use personal and possessive pronouns as subject and object correctly for self- expression

## Introduction
This bandage is mine. Those gloves are hers. The words mine and hers show who owns something without saying the noun again. They are different from my bandage and her gloves.

## Notes
### Belonging without repeating the noun
A possessive pronoun shows that something belongs to someone. It stands alone. It does not come immediately before a noun.

- mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs
- its (for a thing)

This first aid kit is mine. The head lights are ours. The wiper she found is his.

Words such as my, your, our and their do a similar job, but they must be followed by a noun: my wiper, their fog lights. Do not say this wiper is my. Say this wiper is mine. Do not say this is hers book. Say this is her book, or this book is hers.

### As subject and as object
A possessive pronoun can do the action.

- Mine is in the bag.
- Ours has new signal lights.

It can also receive the action.

- I borrowed yours.
- The teacher checked theirs before the trip.

His can be a possessive pronoun or the word before a noun. The signal lights are his. His signal lights are bright. The sentence pattern tells you which job it has.

### Its and it's
Its shows belonging and has no apostrophe: The car lost its wiper.
It's means it is: It's raining, so switch on the head lights.

### A joint reading
Read this short paragraph and listen for pronouns.

Baraka pointed to a car near the bridge. 'Ours is the blue one,' he said. 'Its fog lights are on because the morning is misty. Yours is behind ours. The driver gave me his, I mean the key that is his, so I could lock the door.' Chebet laughed. 'The key is yours now, until you give it back.'

## Key words
• possessive pronoun — a word such as mine, yours or theirs that shows belonging and stands alone
• apostrophe — the mark (') used in it's to show that a letter has been left out
• wiper — the rubber blade that clears rain from a vehicle's windscreen
• head lights — the main lamps at the front of a vehicle, used to see the road

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Choose mine or my: These gloves are ____.

Working:
1. There is no noun after the gap.
2. The standalone possessive pronoun for I is mine.

Answer: These gloves are mine.

### Example 2
Correct: The dog wagged it's tail near the bridge.

Working:
1. The tail belongs to the dog.
2. Belonging uses its, without an apostrophe.

Answer: The dog wagged its tail near the bridge.

### Example 3
Use a possessive pronoun as the subject: The fog lights that belong to us are bright.

Working:
1. The thing that belongs to us can be replaced by ours.
2. Ours becomes the subject.

Answer: Ours are bright.

## Activity: Find the pronouns in a text
You will need: A short newspaper cutting, magazine page or the paragraph about Baraka's car, Coloured pencils
1. Read the text together once.
2. Underline personal pronouns in one colour and possessive pronouns in another.
3. For each possessive pronoun, say whether it is used as a subject or comes after the verb.
4. Type two of your sentences on a word processor, phone or tablet if your teacher provides one. Read them aloud to check the pronouns.

## Practice
1. Write the possessive pronoun for we.
2. Correct the sentence: This bandage is her.
3. Choose its or it's: ____ a new wiper, and the car needs ____ wiper replaced.
4. Is theirs a subject or an object in 'The officer checked theirs'?

## Summary
• Possessive pronouns stand alone: mine, yours, his, hers, its, ours, theirs.
• My, your, her, our and their need a noun after them.
• Its shows belonging. It's means it is.

### Answers to practice
1. ours
2. This bandage is hers.
3. It's a new wiper, and the car needs its wiper replaced.
4. An object. Theirs receives the action of checked.

PAGE 4: Lesson 3: Pronouns with vehicle and road words

LESSON 3: PRONOUNS WITH VEHICLE AND ROAD WORDS
==============================================

## What you will learn
• Build sentences about a vehicle using personal and possessive pronouns.
• Keep the pronoun matched to the person or thing it replaces.
• Use pronouns naturally when talking about safety near a bridge.

Curriculum outcomes: b) use personal and possessive pronouns as subject and object correctly for self- expression; c) adopt the use of personal and possessive pronouns in communication

## Introduction
The words wiper, head lights, signal lights and fog lights are useful, but a sentence still needs to say who switched them on and whose vehicle it is. Pronouns do that cleanly.

## Notes
### Words for this lesson
- A wiper clears rain from the windscreen.
- Head lights are the main front lamps. Drivers use them at night and when rain or dust makes it hard to see.
- Signal lights flash on one side to show that the driver intends to turn or change lane. They are also called indicators.
- Fog lights are extra lamps for fog or very poor visibility. They do not replace head lights on an ordinary clear day.
- A bridge carries a road or path over a river, a railway or another road.

### Building the sentences
Start with names, then shorten with pronouns.

- Mother switched on the head lights. She switched them on.
- The signal lights belong to Father's car. They are his.
- Our fog lights are bright. Ours are bright.
- The mechanic repaired the wiper for the family. He repaired it for us.

Keep the pronoun honest. If the sentence began with Chebet, the next subject is she, not he or they. If the sentence began with the signal lights, the next pronoun is they, because lights are plural.

### A model paragraph
Our car stopped near the bridge because the rain was heavy. Father switched on the head lights, and they cut through the spray. Mother checked the wipers. Hers moved smoothly, but the one on the left was slow, so Father said he would replace it. Chebet pointed to the signal lights. 'Those are ours,' she said. 'Please use them before you turn.' He thanked her. She had reminded him of a safe habit.

### Making pronouns a habit
When you speak, pause if a sentence sounds like 'The teacher gave the chart to I.' Change it before you finish. When you write, read the sentence once and ask: who is doing this, and who receives it? That check will make personal and possessive pronouns part of your ordinary speech, not only a grammar exercise.

## Key words
• signal lights — lamps that flash to show which way a driver intends to turn
• fog lights — extra lamps used when fog or heavy rain makes it hard to see
• bridge — a structure that carries a road or path over a river, railway or another road
• plural — more than one, such as lights or they

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Combine the ideas with pronouns: Amina owns the bicycle. The bicycle is near the bridge. The lamp belongs to Amina.

Working:
1. Amina becomes she.
2. The bicycle can become it.
3. The lamp that belongs to her can be hers.

Answer: Her bicycle is near the bridge. The lamp is hers. Or: Hers is near the bridge, and its lamp is bright.

### Example 2
Fill the gaps: Father flashed the signal lights. ____ flashed ____ before the bridge.

Working:
1. Father is he.
2. The signal lights are they or them. After flashed, use them.

Answer: He flashed them before the bridge.

## Activity: Flash cards beside the bridge
You will need: Flash cards labelled wiper, bridge, head lights, signal lights, fog lights, Paper for sentences
1. Spread out a picture or flash cards of a car near a bridge.
2. In pairs, make five sentences. Use at least one personal pronoun and one possessive pronoun in the set.
3. Read the sentences to another pair. They point to each pronoun and say subject, object or possessive.
4. If a device is available, type your best two sentences and save them to show the class.

## Practice
1. What do signal lights tell other road users?
2. Rewrite using pronouns: Mother and Father checked the fog lights. The fog lights belong to Mother and Father.
3. Choose the correct sentence: 'Them fog lights are bright' or 'Those fog lights are theirs.'

## Summary
• Replace names with he, she, it or they only when the listener knows who or what you mean.
• Use mine, ours, his, hers and theirs to show belonging.
• Signal lights, head lights, fog lights and wipers can all be the it or they of a safety sentence.

### Answers to practice
1. They flash to show that the driver intends to turn or change lane.
2. They checked them. The fog lights are theirs. Or: They checked theirs.
3. Those fog lights are theirs.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 4.3.1 GRAMMAR IN USE: WORD CLASSES (PRONOUNS)
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Which word is a subject pronoun?
   A. me
   B. them
   C. she
   D. hers

2. Choose the correct sentence.
   A. The nurse helped I.
   B. The nurse helped me.
   C. The nurse helped mine.
   D. Me was helped the nurse.

3. Amina and Juma waited. The pronoun for both of them as the subject is
   A. him
   B. them
   C. they
   D. us

4. Which pronoun can stand alone to show belonging to us?
   A. our
   B. ours
   C. we
   D. us

5. Correct choice: The car lost ____ wiper.
   A. it's
   B. its
   C. its'
   D. it

6. 'This kit is hers.' Hers is
   A. a subject pronoun
   B. an object pronoun doing the action
   C. a possessive pronoun
   D. a verb

7. Father switched on the head lights. Which rewrite is correct?
   A. Him switched on they.
   B. He switched them on.
   C. He switched they on.
   D. His switched on he.

8. Fog lights are used mainly
   A. instead of brakes
   B. when fog or very poor visibility makes it hard to see
   C. to show a turn on a clear day
   D. as wipers

9. Which sentence uses a possessive pronoun as the subject?
   A. Ours is near the bridge.
   B. She is near the bridge.
   C. The driver saw us.
   D. Give the key to him.

10. Rewrite correctly: Me and Chebet saw the signal lights.
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 4.3.1 GRAMMAR IN USE: WORD CLASSES (PRONOUNS)
========================================

1. C. she
   She does the action. Me and them are object pronouns. Hers is possessive.

2. B. The nurse helped me.
   Helped is followed by the object pronoun me.

3. C. they
   They replaces Amina and Juma when they do the action.

4. B. ours
   Ours is the possessive pronoun. Our needs a noun, as in our car.

5. B. its
   Its shows belonging. It's means it is.

6. C. a possessive pronoun
   Hers shows that the kit belongs to her and it stands alone.

7. B. He switched them on.
   He is the subject. Them is the object pronoun for the lights.

8. B. when fog or very poor visibility makes it hard to see
   Fog lights help in fog or very poor visibility. Signal lights show a turn.

9. A. Ours is near the bridge.
   Ours means our vehicle or our lights and it does the job of the subject.

10. Chebet and I saw the signal lights.
   The subject form is I, and the other person is named first.

studyPages.title: Lesson 1: Personal pronouns as subjects and objects
studyPages.body:
LESSON 1: PERSONAL PRONOUNS AS SUBJECTS AND OBJECTS
===================================================

## What you will learn
• Identify personal pronouns that do the action and personal pronouns that receive it.
• Replace a noun with the correct subject or object pronoun.
• Correct sentences that use me or I in the wrong place.

Curriculum outcomes: a) identify personal and possessive pronouns used as subjects and objects for communication; b) use personal and possessive pronouns as subject and object correctly for self- expression

## Introduction
Amina helped Juma. She helped him. The second sentence is shorter because she and him stand in for the names. Choosing the wrong pronoun makes the sentence sound unfinished or rude to the ear.

## Notes
### What a personal pronoun does
A personal pronoun takes the place of a person or a thing that has already been named. There are two jobs to learn.

The subject pronoun does the action. It comes before the verb.

- I, you, he, she, it, we, they

The object pronoun receives the action, or comes after a word such as to, for, with or near.

- me, you, him, her, it, us, them

Notice that you and it stay the same. The others change.

### Matching the pronoun
- Amina washed the cut. She washed it.
- The nurse helped Juma. The nurse helped him.
- The teacher called Amina and Juma. The teacher called them.
- Otieno and I carried the kit. We carried it.

Use he, him and his for a boy or a man, she and her for a girl or a woman, and it for one thing or animal when we are not using a personal name. Use they and them for more than one person or thing.

### Two mistakes to avoid
The subject form is I, not me. Say Amina and I saw the bridge, not Me and Amina saw the bridge. Put the other person first: Amina and I, not I and Amina.

The object form is me, him, her, us or them, not the subject form. Say The nurse helped me, not The nurse helped I. Say The motorcycle nearly hit him, not The motorcycle nearly hit he.

### A short scene
Chebet fell near the bridge and cut her knee. Wanjiru ran to her. 'I will call the teacher,' Wanjiru said. The teacher knelt beside them and opened the first aid kit. 'We will clean it,' she said. She did not give them any medicine. An adult does that, if it is needed.

## Key words
• pronoun — a word that takes the place of a noun, such as she or them
• subject pronoun — a pronoun that does the action, such as I, he, she, we or they
• object pronoun — a pronoun that receives the action, such as me, him, her, us or them
• verb — the action word in a sentence, such as helped or washed

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Replace the underlined names: Amina showed Juma the footbridge.

Working:
1. Amina does the action, so use she.
2. Juma receives the showing, so use him.

Answer: She showed him the footbridge.

### Example 2
Choose the correct word: The driver gave the warning to (we / us).

Working:
1. The pronoun comes after to, so it is an object.
2. The object form of we is us.

Answer: The driver gave the warning to us.

### Example 3
Correct this sentence: Me and Otieno told the teacher.

Working:
1. Me cannot be the subject.
2. Name the other person first, then use I.

Answer: Otieno and I told the teacher.

## Activity: Pronouns in a picture talk
You will need: A picture of children near a bridge, with a car and an adult, Sentence strips
1. In groups, look at the picture and name the people and things.
2. Say four sentences about the picture. Each sentence must use a subject pronoun and, where you can, an object pronoun.
3. Write the sentences and underline the pronouns. Mark S for a subject pronoun and O for an object pronoun.
4. Read one sentence aloud and let the group say whether the pronoun is in the right place.

## Practice
1. Write the object pronoun that matches she.
2. Replace the nouns: The doctor examined the patient.
3. Which is correct: 'Them are at the crossing' or 'They are at the crossing'?
4. Fill in: The teacher praised ____ (I / me) for getting help.

## Summary
• Subject pronouns do the action: I, you, he, she, it, we, they.
• Object pronouns receive the action: me, you, him, her, it, us, them.
• Say 'Amina and I', and say 'helped me', not 'helped I'.

### Answers to practice
1. her
2. He examined him, or She examined her, or The doctor examined him or her. A correct pair is: She examined him.
3. They are at the crossing. They is the subject pronoun.
4. me

studyPages.title: Lesson 2: Possessive pronouns
studyPages.body:
LESSON 2: POSSESSIVE PRONOUNS
=============================

## What you will learn
• Tell a possessive pronoun from a word like my or our that needs a noun.
• Use possessive pronouns as the subject or the object of a sentence.
• Choose its or it's correctly.

Curriculum outcomes: a) identify personal and possessive pronouns used as subjects and objects for communication; b) use personal and possessive pronouns as subject and object correctly for self- expression

## Introduction
This bandage is mine. Those gloves are hers. The words mine and hers show who owns something without saying the noun again. They are different from my bandage and her gloves.

## Notes
### Belonging without repeating the noun
A possessive pronoun shows that something belongs to someone. It stands alone. It does not come immediately before a noun.

- mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs
- its (for a thing)

This first aid kit is mine. The head lights are ours. The wiper she found is his.

Words such as my, your, our and their do a similar job, but they must be followed by a noun: my wiper, their fog lights. Do not say this wiper is my. Say this wiper is mine. Do not say this is hers book. Say this is her book, or this book is hers.

### As subject and as object
A possessive pronoun can do the action.

- Mine is in the bag.
- Ours has new signal lights.

It can also receive the action.

- I borrowed yours.
- The teacher checked theirs before the trip.

His can be a possessive pronoun or the word before a noun. The signal lights are his. His signal lights are bright. The sentence pattern tells you which job it has.

### Its and it's
Its shows belonging and has no apostrophe: The car lost its wiper.
It's means it is: It's raining, so switch on the head lights.

### A joint reading
Read this short paragraph and listen for pronouns.

Baraka pointed to a car near the bridge. 'Ours is the blue one,' he said. 'Its fog lights are on because the morning is misty. Yours is behind ours. The driver gave me his, I mean the key that is his, so I could lock the door.' Chebet laughed. 'The key is yours now, until you give it back.'

## Key words
• possessive pronoun — a word such as mine, yours or theirs that shows belonging and stands alone
• apostrophe — the mark (') used in it's to show that a letter has been left out
• wiper — the rubber blade that clears rain from a vehicle's windscreen
• head lights — the main lamps at the front of a vehicle, used to see the road

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Choose mine or my: These gloves are ____.

Working:
1. There is no noun after the gap.
2. The standalone possessive pronoun for I is mine.

Answer: These gloves are mine.

### Example 2
Correct: The dog wagged it's tail near the bridge.

Working:
1. The tail belongs to the dog.
2. Belonging uses its, without an apostrophe.

Answer: The dog wagged its tail near the bridge.

### Example 3
Use a possessive pronoun as the subject: The fog lights that belong to us are bright.

Working:
1. The thing that belongs to us can be replaced by ours.
2. Ours becomes the subject.

Answer: Ours are bright.

## Activity: Find the pronouns in a text
You will need: A short newspaper cutting, magazine page or the paragraph about Baraka's car, Coloured pencils
1. Read the text together once.
2. Underline personal pronouns in one colour and possessive pronouns in another.
3. For each possessive pronoun, say whether it is used as a subject or comes after the verb.
4. Type two of your sentences on a word processor, phone or tablet if your teacher provides one. Read them aloud to check the pronouns.

## Practice
1. Write the possessive pronoun for we.
2. Correct the sentence: This bandage is her.
3. Choose its or it's: ____ a new wiper, and the car needs ____ wiper replaced.
4. Is theirs a subject or an object in 'The officer checked theirs'?

## Summary
• Possessive pronouns stand alone: mine, yours, his, hers, its, ours, theirs.
• My, your, her, our and their need a noun after them.
• Its shows belonging. It's means it is.

### Answers to practice
1. ours
2. This bandage is hers.
3. It's a new wiper, and the car needs its wiper replaced.
4. An object. Theirs receives the action of checked.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Pronouns with vehicle and road words
studyPages.body:
LESSON 3: PRONOUNS WITH VEHICLE AND ROAD WORDS
==============================================

## What you will learn
• Build sentences about a vehicle using personal and possessive pronouns.
• Keep the pronoun matched to the person or thing it replaces.
• Use pronouns naturally when talking about safety near a bridge.

Curriculum outcomes: b) use personal and possessive pronouns as subject and object correctly for self- expression; c) adopt the use of personal and possessive pronouns in communication

## Introduction
The words wiper, head lights, signal lights and fog lights are useful, but a sentence still needs to say who switched them on and whose vehicle it is. Pronouns do that cleanly.

## Notes
### Words for this lesson
- A wiper clears rain from the windscreen.
- Head lights are the main front lamps. Drivers use them at night and when rain or dust makes it hard to see.
- Signal lights flash on one side to show that the driver intends to turn or change lane. They are also called indicators.
- Fog lights are extra lamps for fog or very poor visibility. They do not replace head lights on an ordinary clear day.
- A bridge carries a road or path over a river, a railway or another road.

### Building the sentences
Start with names, then shorten with pronouns.

- Mother switched on the head lights. She switched them on.
- The signal lights belong to Father's car. They are his.
- Our fog lights are bright. Ours are bright.
- The mechanic repaired the wiper for the family. He repaired it for us.

Keep the pronoun honest. If the sentence began with Chebet, the next subject is she, not he or they. If the sentence began with the signal lights, the next pronoun is they, because lights are plural.

### A model paragraph
Our car stopped near the bridge because the rain was heavy. Father switched on the head lights, and they cut through the spray. Mother checked the wipers. Hers moved smoothly, but the one on the left was slow, so Father said he would replace it. Chebet pointed to the signal lights. 'Those are ours,' she said. 'Please use them before you turn.' He thanked her. She had reminded him of a safe habit.

### Making pronouns a habit
When you speak, pause if a sentence sounds like 'The teacher gave the chart to I.' Change it before you finish. When you write, read the sentence once and ask: who is doing this, and who receives it? That check will make personal and possessive pronouns part of your ordinary speech, not only a grammar exercise.

## Key words
• signal lights — lamps that flash to show which way a driver intends to turn
• fog lights — extra lamps used when fog or heavy rain makes it hard to see
• bridge — a structure that carries a road or path over a river, railway or another road
• plural — more than one, such as lights or they

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Combine the ideas with pronouns: Amina owns the bicycle. The bicycle is near the bridge. The lamp belongs to Amina.

Working:
1. Amina becomes she.
2. The bicycle can become it.
3. The lamp that belongs to her can be hers.

Answer: Her bicycle is near the bridge. The lamp is hers. Or: Hers is near the bridge, and its lamp is bright.

### Example 2
Fill the gaps: Father flashed the signal lights. ____ flashed ____ before the bridge.

Working:
1. Father is he.
2. The signal lights are they or them. After flashed, use them.

Answer: He flashed them before the bridge.

## Activity: Flash cards beside the bridge
You will need: Flash cards labelled wiper, bridge, head lights, signal lights, fog lights, Paper for sentences
1. Spread out a picture or flash cards of a car near a bridge.
2. In pairs, make five sentences. Use at least one personal pronoun and one possessive pronoun in the set.
3. Read the sentences to another pair. They point to each pronoun and say subject, object or possessive.
4. If a device is available, type your best two sentences and save them to show the class.

## Practice
1. What do signal lights tell other road users?
2. Rewrite using pronouns: Mother and Father checked the fog lights. The fog lights belong to Mother and Father.
3. Choose the correct sentence: 'Them fog lights are bright' or 'Those fog lights are theirs.'

## Summary
• Replace names with he, she, it or they only when the listener knows who or what you mean.
• Use mine, ours, his, hers and theirs to show belonging.
• Signal lights, head lights, fog lights and wipers can all be the it or they of a safety sentence.

### Answers to practice
1. They flash to show that the driver intends to turn or change lane.
2. They checked them. The fog lights are theirs. Or: They checked theirs.
3. Those fog lights are theirs.

questions.question: Which word is a subject pronoun?
questions.explanation: She does the action. Me and them are object pronouns. Hers is possessive.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: Helped is followed by the object pronoun me.

questions.question: Amina and Juma waited. The pronoun for both of them as the subject is
questions.explanation: They replaces Amina and Juma when they do the action.

questions.question: Which pronoun can stand alone to show belonging to us?
questions.explanation: Ours is the possessive pronoun. Our needs a noun, as in our car.

questions.question: Correct choice: The car lost ____ wiper.
questions.explanation: Its shows belonging. It's means it is.

questions.question: 'This kit is hers.' Hers is
options: an object pronoun doing the action
questions.explanation: Hers shows that the kit belongs to her and it stands alone.

questions.question: Father switched on the head lights. Which rewrite is correct?
questions.explanation: He is the subject. Them is the object pronoun for the lights.

questions.question: Fog lights are used mainly
options: when fog or very poor visibility makes it hard to see
to show a turn on a clear day
questions.explanation: Fog lights help in fog or very poor visibility. Signal lights show a turn.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a possessive pronoun as the subject?
questions.explanation: Ours means our vehicle or our lights and it does the job of the subject.

questions.question: Rewrite correctly: Me and Chebet saw the signal lights.
questions.answer: Chebet and I saw the signal lights.
questions.explanation: The subject form is I, and the other person is named first.
